title: Thanthai Periyar and the Railway Guard: Reason and Human Dignity Over Privilege
summary: During a train journey in early 20th century Tamil Nadu, Thanthai Periyar used brilliant common-sense logic to challenge caste-based segregation in public compartments.
keywords: Historical Dialogue 146: லிங்கனும் மதகுரு ஜே.பி. கல்லிவரும்: பேச்சின் ரகசியம் என்ன?
full_text:
In the early 1930s, Periyar E. V. Ramasamy was constantly crisscrossing the towns and villages of South India by train to advocate for the Self-Respect Movement.

On one journey in a crowded third-class compartment, an orthodox high-caste traveler boarded the carriage. Observing Periyar’s rustic khadi attire, long white beard, and unassuming demeanor, the man assumed he belonged to a lower social stratum and immediately took offense.

When the train guard passed through the carriage, the orthodox passenger complained loudly:
"Guard! It is intolerable that people of all descriptions are allowed to sit in this compartment. My ritual purity is compromised. Shift these common folk elsewhere!"

The guard hesitated, but Periyar calmly looked up, smiled with disarming warmth, and addressed the passenger:
"My friend, I admire your passion for ritual, but consider the physical reality of our situation. This locomotive was forged from iron by laborers; it is powered by black coal shoveled by soot-covered workmen. Furthermore, observe the air flowing through these open windows: the oxygen you inhale has passed through my lungs, and the air I exhale enters yours!
If nature itself refuses to practice untouchability in the very air we breathe to stay alive, by what logic can human beings claim superiority over one another in a public railway coach? We were all born equal, and we all depart this earth equal!"

The compartment erupted in spontaneous laughter and applause. Disarmed by Periyar’s clear scientific logic, the passenger quietly sat down. Rationalism had once again prevailed through wit and reason.
